moduleTitle: Integrating Testim with Azure DevOps & GitHub Actions for streamlined test results
learningObjectives: Set up a GitHub Actions workflow that installs the Testim CLI and runs tests.
Trigger Testim runs from Azure DevOps release pipelines.
Explain how GitHub branch activity is mirrored into Testim.

elements.description: Integrating Testim with GitHub Actions means creating a GitHub Actions workflow that sets up Node.js and installs the Testim CLI, then runs it as a step in the workflow — the same CLI used for any other CI integration, just wired into GitHub's own workflow syntax.

Separately from Actions, Testim's GitHub integration mirrors version-control activity: branches created in GitHub are automatically created in Testim under the same name, and merging branches in GitHub automatically merges the corresponding branches in Testim — keeping test versions aligned with code versions without manual syncing.

bulletPoints: GitHub Actions: a workflow installs Node.js + the Testim CLI, then runs it as a step.
GitHub branch integration: branches and merges in GitHub are auto-mirrored into Testim.

elements.description: Testim runs can be fired from Azure DevOps (as well as Jenkins, GitHub Actions, and GitLab CI), letting a release pipeline trigger Testim execution as part of its normal deployment flow rather than as a disconnected, manually-run step.

elements.text: This is the same underlying pattern as GitHub Actions and Jenkins — the CI/CD tool calls into the Testim CLI/API as a pipeline step — Azure DevOps is just one more platform this generalizes to.

bulletPoints: Azure DevOps release pipelines can trigger Testim runs directly.
Same underlying mechanism generalizes across Jenkins, GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps, and GitLab CI.

examPitfalls.title: Confusing GitHub Actions integration with GitHub branch integration
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming setting up a GitHub Actions workflow automatically also mirrors branches/merges into Testim, or vice versa.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: GitHub Actions integration is about running the Testim CLI as a workflow step to execute tests. GitHub branch integration is a separate mechanism that auto-mirrors branch creation and merges from GitHub into Testim.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What does a GitHub Actions workflow need to set up before it can run Testim tests?

options.text: Nothing — Testim runs natively in GitHub Actions with no setup.

practiceQuiz.hint: Same CLI as everywhere else, so it needs the same runtime.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Integrating Testim with GitHub Actions means creating a workflow with Node.js and installing the Testim CLI — since the CLI is a Node.js/npm package, that runtime is a prerequisite.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What happens in Testim when a branch is created and later merged in GitHub, assuming GitHub integration is set up?

options.text: Nothing — GitHub branches have no relationship to Testim branches.
The branch is automatically created in Testim under the same name, and merging in GitHub automatically merges it in Testim too.
The entire Testim project is deleted and recreated.
A manual export/import step is required each time.

practiceQuiz.hint: It's an automatic mirroring, not a manual process.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Branches created in GitHub are automatically created in Testim under the same name, and merging branches in GitHub automatically merges the branches in Testim — no manual export/import needed.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which of the following can trigger a Testim run from a release pipeline?

options.text: Azure DevOps, Jenkins, GitHub Actions, and GitLab CI.
Only Azure DevOps — no other platform supports this.
Only a manual click inside the Testim editor.
This capability doesn't exist in Testim.

practiceQuiz.hint: It's the same set of major CI/CD platforms named throughout this integrations section.
practiceQuiz.rationale: You can fire Testim runs from Azure DevOps, Jenkins, GitHub Actions, and GitLab CI, triggering them directly from release pipelines rather than needing a manual run.

quickRecap.value: Workflow installs Node.js + Testim CLI, then runs it as a step.
Branch creation/merges in GitHub auto-mirror into Testim.
Release pipelines can trigger Testim runs directly, same pattern as Jenkins/GitHub Actions/GitLab CI.
